map.summary: The evaluation subsystem loads hash-verified, versioned datasets, prepares isolated per-scope evaluation corpora in OpenSearch through the durable ingestion pipeline, runs bm25/dense/hybrid/hybrid_rerank retrieval via a shared EvaluationSearch boundary, scores rankings with fixed metrics, and emits reproducible comparison reports. It exposes a debug-only search API and a SciFact builder CLI, and owns evaluation ORM tables.
unknowns: Runtime wiring between the evaluation ORM models and the dataset loader is not observed (F0080).
How the runner's OpenSearch read-alias lookup (F0039) relates to corpus alias derivation beyond the shared read-alias name (F0008, F0075).
Error-code contracts exposed to callers for the debug endpoint beyond HTTP status mapping (F0004, F0092).
Concurrency/ORDM behavior of inline durable jobs under real ingestion workers or the ingestion worker service (F0010, F0015).
Whether the EvaluationSearch module docstring's shared HTTP-and-runner boundary is enforced structurally or only by convention (F0062, uncertain).

diagrams.title: Architecture
diagrams.description: Evaluation composes dataset loading, corpus preparation, mode-dispatch search, scoring/reporting, its HTTP and CLI entry points, and persistence; boundaries matter because corpus state and retrieval faults map to distinct errors.

diagrams.title: Corpus preparation flow
diagrams.description: prepare_corpus derives a deterministic scope and index aliases, reuses the durable ingestion pipeline inline, treats persisted documents as immutable, then force-merges and verifies against job receipts.

diagrams.title: Evaluation run flow
diagrams.description: run_baseline selects and prepares a dataset, calls evaluate across modes, scores each ranking against judgments, attaches credential-free reproduction metadata, and writes JSON plus markdown reports.

diagrams.title: Search mode dispatch
diagrams.description: EvaluationSearch validates mode and filters, fixes a benchmark budget, lazy-builds the mode-specific retriever, then asserts every result stays inside the resolved scope before deduplicating documents.

diagrams.title: SciFact dataset build
diagrams.description: The SciFact CLI verifies a pinned archive download, converts BEIR files into the shared four-file contract, and can build a deterministic 30-query/500-doc subset that load_dataset re-validates.

F0001.statement: The evaluation package's public surface (S0001) re-exports the versioned dataset contracts (CorpusRecord, DatasetManifest, EvaluationDataset, JudgmentRecord, QueryRecord) and load_dataset from hybrid_rag_search.evaluation.datasets; numbered-day comments indicate contracts and loaders are the package's core abstraction.

F0002.statement: api.py exposes a single local-only debug endpoint POST /debug/search (S0002) that rejects requests when settings.app_env == "production" with HTTP 404, gating the evaluation search surface out of production deployments.

F0003.statement: debug_search orchestrates the full evaluation search path inline: selected_dataset(name) loads the dataset, verify_prepared(dataset, settings) validates the prepared corpus, then EvaluationSearch(settings) is used as an async context manager to run search(dataset, query, mode, debug=True) (S0002).

F0004.statement: debug_search maps failures to distinct HTTP boundaries: ValueError/OSError become 409 (state conflict), while RetrievalError and ProviderError become 503 with error.code, keeping retrieval/provider faults separate from corpus-state faults (S0002).

F0005.statement: corpus.py defines a fixed evaluation tenant EVALUATION_TENANT (UUID ...0201) and a DATASETS mapping of three named datasets: synthetic-workspace, scifact, and scifact-subset; selected_dataset resolves names against this mapping and raises ValueError on unknown names (S0003).

F0006.statement: evaluation_scope derives a deterministic EvaluationScope: collection_id is uuid5 of the evaluation tenant plus the dataset corpus_hash and configured pipeline version, and each document id is uuid5 of the collection id plus the record id, so the same dataset/pipeline yields the same scope (S0003).

F0007.statement: Evaluation scopes are restricted to document corpora: evaluation_scope raises ValueError if any corpus record.type != "document", and comments state Day 15 evaluates document corpora only (S0003).

F0008.statement: evaluation_index_settings derives per-scope OpenSearch read/write alias names of the form hybrid-rag-eval-{collection_id}-read/-write, deliberately isolated from demo aliases and manual rebuilds (S0003).

F0009.statement: ensure_evaluation_index HEAD-checks the physical index hybrid-rag-eval-{collection_id} and, only when absent (404), creates it via OpenSearchIndexManager and then points the write alias and promotes the read alias (S0003).

F0010.statement: prepare_corpus reuses the durable ingestion pipeline rather than a bespoke path: it creates a Tenant and Collection row (conflict-ignoring inserts), persists document bytes via LocalFileStorage with a content-hash check, enqueues jobs through IngestionJobService with a no-op ManualPublisher, and runs them inline via run_configured_job with a ManualActor (S0003).

F0011.statement: prepare_corpus treats previously persisted documents as immutable-per-dataset: if an existing Document's content_hash or source_metadata differs from the dataset record it raises ValueError ("Prepared evaluation document differs from dataset") instead of overwriting (S0003).

F0012.statement: prepare_corpus ensures pipeline completeness before returning: it calls compact_corpus (OpenSearch _forcemerge with max_num_segments=1) and then verify_prepared, so corpus preparation ends with a forced-merged and verified index (S0003).

F0013.statement: verify_prepared performs two-phase validation that fails closed: it queries Postgres for succeeded IngestionJob rows matching tenant, document ids, and pipeline version, requires a valid index receipt (generation_id string, integer chunk_count) per job, then aggregates OpenSearch ready-visibility documents by document_id/generation_id and requires exact equality with expected generations and doc counts (S0003).

F0014.statement: prepare_corpus used inside verify_prepared/debug_search relies on the durable ingestion records (IngestionJob.checkpoint["index"] receipts) as the source of truth for OpenSearch index contents, coupling the evaluation subsystem's integrity check to the ingestion subsystem's bookkeeping (S0003).

F0015.statement: prepare_corpus supports an explicit document_delay parameter (sleeping between documents) and raises ValueError for negative values, and ManualActor/ManualPublisher are documented as executing durable jobs inline with retries left explicit (S0003).

F0016.statement: The evaluation subsystem's external integrations observed in these sources are Postgres via SQLAlchemy async engine/sessionmaker and OpenSearch over httpx (index HEAD/create/forcemerge/_search), with local document bytes owned by LocalFileStorage; settings for OpenSearch aliases, url, and embedding dimensions are threaded through Settings objects (S0002, S0003).

F0017.statement: load_dataset(directory) is the public entry point of evaluation/datasets.py: it reads manifest.json as a DatasetManifest, then reads corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, and judgments.jsonl into typed Pydantic records, returning an EvaluationDataset with computed corpus_hash and dataset_hash.

F0018.statement: Dataset files are integrity-checked before parsing: for each manifest.files entry, load_dataset computes SHA-256 of the file bytes and raises DatasetValidationError on mismatch with the declared entry.sha256.

F0019.statement: DatasetManifest bounds the dataset to exactly the files corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, and judgments.jsonl exactly once via the require_all_files_once model validator; DatasetFile.path is a Literal restricted to those three names.

F0020.statement: All dataset models inherit StrictModel (ConfigDict extra="forbid", frozen=True), so unknown JSON fields are rejected and loaded records are immutable; DatasetValidationError is the single error type raised for validation failures.

F0021.statement: load_dataset performs cross-record validation beyond schema: it enforces unique corpus and query ids (_unique_ids), requires each judgment.query_id to reference a known query, requires each judgment.target_id to exist in the corpus, and requires the referenced corpus record's type to match judgment.target_type.

F0022.statement: load_dataset enforces two coverage invariants over queries: every query must have at least one judgment, and every query must have at least one judgment with relevance_grade > 0.

F0023.statement: CorpusRecord enforces parentage by type: records of type 'chunk' require document_id, and records of type 'document' must not set document_id.

F0024.statement: EvaluationDataset.dataset_hash is not a file hash but a digest over a canonical joined string of schema_version, dataset_id, version, and the sorted '<filename>:<sha256>' pairs, making it a deterministic identity for the dataset version.

F0025.statement: JSONL parsing rejects blank lines and non-object lines with DatasetValidationError annotated by filename and 1-based line number, wrapping json.JSONDecodeError and pydantic ValidationError.

F0026.statement: score_ranking(ranking, judgments) is the public scoring entry point in evaluation/metrics.py; it validates that all grades are integers in [0,3] and that at least one positive judgment exists, otherwise raising ValueError.

F0027.statement: score_ranking deduplicates the ranking with dict.fromkeys before applying cutoffs, so a repeated document id only counts once at its first position.

F0028.statement: score_ranking emits recall@5, recall@10, recall@50, mrr@10, and ndcg@10; recall uses the count of distinct relevant documents in the top-cutoff as numerator, and mrr@10 takes the reciprocal rank of the first relevant document within the top 10 else 0.0.

F0029.statement: ndcg@10 is computed with graded DCG (2**grade - 1)/log2(rank+1) over the top 10 retrieved documents, using judgments.get(key, 0) so unjudged results contribute no gain, normalized by the ideal DCG of the top 10 highest grades.

F0030.statement: The datasets module imports only stdlib and pydantic; it has no imports from the ingestion, retrieval, or OpenSearch layers, so the loader is a self-contained boundary that depends on other evaluation modules only via the returned EvaluationDataset (inference).

F0031.statement: The metrics module takes plain inputs (a sequence of ranking strings and a mapping of document id to integer grade) and returns a dict of metric names to floats, with no dependency on the dataset loader's record types or on any retrieval backend.

F0032.statement: The cutoff set is fixed and hardcoded in score_ranking (5, 10, 50 for recall; 10 for mrr and ndcg), with no parameterization in the excerpt.

F0033.statement: The evaluation runner's `run_baseline` orchestrates retrieval benchmarking: it derives benchmark settings via `benchmark_settings(get_settings())`, selects a dataset with `selected_dataset(name)`, applies `evaluation_index_settings`, verifies prepared corpus chunks via `verify_prepared`, then runs `evaluate` through an async `EvaluationSearch` context and writes reports via `save_report`.

F0034.statement: `evaluate` iterates over every query in the dataset and over each mode in `MODES`, calling the injected async `search` function per (query, mode) and timing each call with `perf_counter`; it is decoupled from the concrete search implementation via the `SearchFunction` type alias.

F0035.statement: For each result, `evaluate` trims the returned `chunks` to only `chunk_id`, `evaluation_document_id`, `rank`, and `score`, explicitly to avoid repeating source bytes across many benchmark queries (corpus text is already versioned).

F0036.statement: `evaluate` uses `score_ranking(ranking, judgments[query.id])` where `ranking` is the list of `document_id` values from `result['documents']`, and computes each non-bm25 mode's `delta_vs_bm25` by subtracting the bm25 metric values, making bm25 the reference baseline.

F0037.statement: `evaluate` validates judgments by rejecting any judgment whose `target_type` is not `'document'` or whose `target_id` is duplicated within a query, raising `ValueError('Evaluation requires unique document judgments per query')`, and also rejects a negative `query_delay`.

F0038.statement: `evaluate` aggregates per-mode metrics as the arithmetic mean across all query rows, and supports an optional per-query `query_delay` applied via `asyncio.sleep` before each query's mode loop.

F0039.statement: `run_baseline` queries the OpenSearch read alias over HTTP with `httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=settings.opensearch_url)` issuing `GET /_alias/{settings.opensearch_read_alias}` and records the sorted returned index names into report metadata as `index`.

F0040.statement: `run_baseline` shells out to `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git diff HEAD --name-only` via `subprocess.check_output` to record `code_revision` and `tracked_worktree_dirty` in the reproducibility metadata.

F0041.statement: The report metadata emitted by `run_baseline` captures dataset identity and hashes (`dataset_id`, `version`, `dataset_hash`, `corpus_hash`), resolved `tenant_id`/`collection_id`, `pipeline_version`, hardware details from `platform`/`os`, model names (`cohere_embed_model`, `cohere_rerank_model`), adapter descriptors, and the declared execution mode string ('sequential queries and modes; hybrid branches concurrent; no query embedding cache').

F0042.statement: `configuration(settings)` builds an explicit allowlist of settings names (all `opensearch_bm25_*` fields plus a fixed list of dense, rerank, and timeout settings), with a comment stating this prevents credentials and unrelated settings from entering reports, and appends a hard-coded `rrf_rank_constant: 60`.

F0043.statement: `save_report` runs the report through `jsonable_encoder`, creates the output directory, and writes two files: `report.json` (sorted, indented JSON) and `report.md` rendered by `markdown_report`.

F0044.statement: `compare_reports` enforces repeatability preconditions by raising `ValueError` when metadata keys (`dataset`, `configuration`, `pipeline_version`, `index`, `models`, `adapters`) differ or when query-id sets differ, then returns the maximum absolute per-query and aggregate metric deltas while marking latency as descriptive with no equality requirement.

F0045.statement: The module's `main()` exposes an argparse CLI with subcommands `prepare`, `run`, `compare`, and `export`; `prepare` calls `prepare_corpus`, `run` calls `run_baseline`, `export` re-saves a JSON report, and `compare` prints `compare_reports` output as JSON.

F0046.statement: `run_baseline` counts rerank fallbacks across all queries by summing rows where `row['modes']['hybrid_rerank']['search']['trace']['fallback_reason']` is not None, indicating the search result carries a `trace` with a `fallback_reason` field.

F0047.statement: `markdown_report` emits a fixed metric column set (recall@5, recall@10, recall@50, mrr@10, ndcg@10), presents per-query differences only for `MODES[1:]` against BM25, and documents that JSON includes winning chunks, complete chunk rankings, timings, and traces with unjudged documents scored as zero.

F0048.statement: The runner depends on the evaluation corpus, datasets, metrics, and search modules (`prepare_corpus`, `verify_prepared`, `selected_dataset`, `evaluation_index_settings`, `evaluation_scope`, `EvaluationDataset`, `score_ranking`, `MODES`, `EvaluationSearch`, `benchmark_settings`, `Settings`), so the runner is the top-level orchestrator over dataset loading, corpus preparation, mode dispatch, and scoring; the internal behavior of those modules is not shown in this excerpt.

F0049.statement: The evaluation subsystem has two external entry points in this batch: a four-command-aware argparse CLI in scifact.py (choices: download, validate, subset) and a programmatic EvaluationSearch boundary documented as shared by HTTP and the benchmark runner.

F0050.statement: scifact.py's CLI dispatches 'download' to download_archive then convert_archive, and 'subset' to build_subset; the 'validate' choice exists in the parser but no branch handles it explicitly in main().

F0051.statement: download_archive fetches SCIFACT_URL via httpx with follow_redirects and a 60s timeout into a '.partial' temp file, verifies SHA-256 against the pinned SCIFACT_ARCHIVE_SHA256, and only then atomically replace()s the destination.

F0052.statement: convert_archive re-verifies the archive hash before reading, then converts BEIR SciFact test files (qrels/test.tsv, corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl) into the shared four-file contract (corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, judgments.jsonl, manifest.json) with 'scifact-doc-'/'scifact-query-' ID prefixes and a schema_version of 'evaluation-dataset-v1'.

F0053.statement: convert_archive sets judgment relevance_grade to 3 when the qrels score is >0 and 0 otherwise, collapsing SciFact's graded qrels into a binary grade.

F0054.statement: build_subset selects 30 queries and 500 documents by stable salted SHA-256 ordering over a 'scifact-subset-v1:' salt, requires at least 30 queries and 500 corpus docs, and refuses if the selected judgment targets exceed 500 documents.

F0055.statement: Both convert_archive and build_subset write a manifest whose 'files' entries are per-file SHA-256 digests, and build_subset re-validates its output by calling load_dataset(output) before returning.

F0056.statement: EvaluationSearch.search enforces mode membership in MODES and rejects filter keys outside {source_type, author, source_date_from, source_date_to}.

F0057.statement: EvaluationSearch lazy-initializes mode-specific retrievers: bm25 uses self.lexical directly; dense/hybrid lazily enter configured_cohere_embeddings and build OpenSearchDenseRetriever and HybridRetriever; hybrid_rerank additionally lazily enters configured_cohere_reranking and builds RerankedRetriever, all tracked on an AsyncExitStack.

F0058.statement: EvaluationSearch.search derives scope and index settings per call via evaluation_scope(dataset, self.settings) and evaluation_index_settings(dataset, self.settings), and reassigns self.lexical.read_alias and self.dense.read_alias from the configured opensearch_read_alias.

F0059.statement: EvaluationSearch.search calls benchmark_settings, which model_copies Settings to fix opensearch_bm25_candidate_limit, opensearch_dense_candidate_limit, rerank_candidate_limit, and rerank_result_limit all to BUDGET=100, so evaluation retrievers run with a fixed budget independent of production settings.

F0060.statement: After retrieval, EvaluationSearch.search validates every evidence item against scope by checking tenant_id, collection_id, document_id membership in scope.document_ids, and pipeline_version, raising ValueError on any out-of-scope result.

F0061.statement: EvaluationSearch.search maps retrieved chunks to evaluation document IDs (scope.document_ids[str(item.document_id)]) and deduplicates documents by that ID into a documents list with unique rank, while keeping the full chunks list.

F0062.statement: EvaluationSearch constructs the docstring-implied shared boundary for HTTP and the benchmark runner: the module docstring states it is 'One evaluation search boundary shared by HTTP and the benchmark runner', and the class docstring notes it shares provider resources across queries without caching query embeddings.

F0063.statement: Hybrid RRF is configured with RRFConfig(candidate_limit=BUDGET), tying hybrid candidate limits to the same fixed BUDGET=100 used for retrieval defaults.

F0064.statement: scifact.py's CLI computes _summary(output) which calls load_dataset(directory) and prints dataset id/version, corpus/query/judgment counts, and corpus_hash/dataset_hash, so every successful CLI run ends by re-validating the produced dataset.

F0065.statement: models/evaluation.py defines SQLAlchemy ORM models EvaluationDataset, Judgment, EvaluationRun, and AuditEvent, all inheriting from the shared Base in hybrid_rag_search.database, making the evaluation subsystem the owner of the evaluation_datasets, judgments, evaluation_runs, and audit_events tables.

F0066.statement: Judgment and EvaluationRun both reference evaluation_datasets via composite ForeignKeyConstraint on (tenant_id, dataset_id), enforcing tenant-scoped referential integrity; EvaluationRun additionally references retrieval_configs on (tenant_id, retrieval_config_id) with ondelete RESTRICT, so retrieval configs backing runs cannot be deleted.

F0067.statement: EvaluationRunStatus enumerates queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled and is enforced both by the Python StrEnum and a SQL CheckConstraint (status_allowed) on evaluation_runs, plus DEFAULT queued via server_default.

F0068.statement: EvaluationDataset persists a corpus_hash column constrained by a regex CheckConstraint requiring a 64-hex-character SHA-256 pattern, tying persisted datasets to content-addressed corpus identity.

F0069.statement: EvaluationRun separates a metrics JSONB object column from status/error_message/started_at/finished_at/updated_at columns, indicating a state-machine lifecycle is tracked at the row level rather than in a separate job table.

F0070.statement: AuditEvent enforces an action format CheckConstraint matching a namespaced pattern '<ns>.<action>' and an entity_type pattern, and links tenant-scoped actor_membership_id to memberships; it does not reference any evaluation-specific table by foreign key, so audit events reference evaluation entities only via entity_type/entity_id strings.

F0071.statement: test_evaluation_corpus.py exercises corpus.prepare_corpus performing: selecting a synthetic dataset, computing evaluation_scope, writing document content to LocalFileStorage, enqueuing an IngestionJobService.enqueue_document job, invoking run_configured_job, and depositing an IngestionJob row via session.add with a deterministic UUID5 document id derived from collection_id and the dataset record id.

F0072.statement: corpus.prepare_corpus is idempotent for already-prepared documents: when the persisted IngestionJob exists and enqueue status is 'succeeded', run_configured_job is not awaited and session.add is not called (test asserts neither ran).

F0073.statement: corpus.prepare_corpus raises ValueError when a persisted document's content_hash differs from the on-disk content in LocalFileStorage, and raises when the enqueued job returns JobRunResult.RETRY_SCHEDULED, and rejects negative document_delay.

F0074.statement: corpus.verify_prepared requires every scoped document to have an IngestionJob row with a non-empty checkpoint containing index.generation_id and chunk_count (a 'receipt'), and then queries OpenSearch via httpx.AsyncClient aggregation buckets per document key, raising ValueError when generations differ.

F0075.statement: corpus.ensure_evaluation_index conditionally calls OpenSearchIndexManager().create: a 404 response triggers create once, while a 200 response on subsequent calls does not re-create, and evaluation index settings use an opensearch_read_alias prefixed 'hybrid-rag-eval-'.

F0076.statement: evaluation.datasets.load_dataset validates dataset directories end-to-end: manifest file list, per-file SHA-256 hash match, JSONL object shape (rejecting arrays, blank lines, and non-JSON), judgment referential integrity (unknown query, unknown target, target type mismatch), duplicate query IDs, queries without any judgment, and queries lacking at least one positive-grade judgment.

F0077.statement: DatasetManifest enforces exactly the expected file set ('files must contain'), and CorpusRecord enforces chunk vs document shape: chunk records require document_id while document records must not have document_id.

F0078.statement: evaluation.metrics.score_ranking returns recall@5/recall@10/recall@50/mrr@10/ndcg@10; it removes duplicate ids before cutoffs, keeps the full judgment denominator when results are short, treats unjudged results as zero-relevance, returns all-zero scores for empty rankings, and raises ValueError for grades outside the integer range 0..3 (rejecting booleans).

F0079.statement: The evaluation subsystem composes with ingestion (IngestionJob, IngestionJobService, JobRunResult, run_configured_job) and retrieval (retrieval_configs foreign key, EvaluationSearch) rather than re-implementing them, as seen in the corpus tests' imports and the EvaluationRun FK to retrieval_configs.

F0080.statement: The ORM model classes in models/evaluation.py and the in-memory dataset loader in evaluation.datasets appear to serve different persistence layers — the loader returns validated Pydantic/domain objects while the models persist rows — but no direct call wiring between them is shown in these excerpts.

F0081.statement: The evaluation runner's run_baseline(name, output_dir, cache_state, count) invokes evaluate(dataset, search) for each query mode, scores rankings, attaches reproduction metadata, and persists report.json and report.md via save_report; tests patch runner.evaluate with AsyncMock to exercise only the surrounding orchestration and metadata persistence (S0013).

F0082.statement: run_baseline records reproduction metadata including code_revision via a subprocess rev-parse call, tracked_worktree_dirty from git status output, cache_state, platform/processor values, and adapter names (e.g. embedding=cohere), and the saved report is asserted not to contain an injected secret value, separating reproduction metadata from credentials (S0013).

F0083.statement: compare_reports enforces comparability across metadata (models) and query sets by raising ValueError with messages 'models' and 'query sets' on mismatches, and reports a max_absolute_per_query_metric_delta field used to assert deterministic runs differ by 0 (S0013).

F0084.statement: evaluate validates dataset uniqueness (duplicate judgments raise ValueError matching 'unique'), rejects negative query_delay with ValueError matching 'nonnegative', and when query_delay is supplied awaits asyncio.sleep with that value between queries, making pacing explicit (S0013).

F0085.statement: save_report writes report.json (structured per-query per-mode deltas such as delta_vs_bm25) and report.md (containing a 'Per-query differences' section) into the provided output directory (S0013).

F0086.statement: evaluation_scope derives a stable scope from dataset and settings: changing dataset_hash does not change the scope, while changing corpus_hash or opensearch_index_schema_version does; the scope exposes tenant_id, collection_id, pipeline_version, and document_ids (8 in the fixture) (S0013).

F0087.statement: evaluation_scope rejects corpora containing non-document record types (a record with type='chunk' raises ValueError matching 'document corpora'), constraining the scope to document-level corpora (S0013).

F0088.statement: benchmark_settings raises rerank_candidate_limit and rerank_result_limit to 100 (versus the default Settings value of 20 for rerank_candidate_limit) for evaluation runs, and configuration(settings) deliberately omits secrets such as cohere_api_key (S0013).

F0089.statement: EvaluationSearch.search(dataset, query, mode, filters) accepts the four modes in MODES, dispatches to BM25, dense, or hybrid retrievers constructed via from_settings (OpenSearchBM25Retriever / OpenSearchDenseRetriever), and asserts that every outgoing OpenSearch request body serializes the scope's tenant_id and collection_id as filters (S0014).

F0090.statement: EvaluationSearch validates mode and filters: an unknown mode raises ValueError matching 'Unknown search', a user-supplied tenant_id filter raises ValueError matching 'Unsupported', and a hit whose tenant_id falls outside the resolved scope raises ValueError matching 'outside' (S0014).

F0091.statement: EvaluationSearch converts OpenSearch chunk hits into results containing both raw chunks and a deduplicated documents list with document_id, chunk_id, and rank, honoring scope.document_ids mapping when building the documents output (S0014).

F0092.statement: The debug endpoint POST /debug/search resolves the dataset, calls verify_prepared, and runs EvaluationSearch across all modes; it returns 422 for unknown datasets or disallowed tenant_id, 404 when app_env is 'production', 409 when verify_prepared raises (not prepared), and 503 when verify_prepared raises RetrievalError(retryable=True) or ProviderError('unavailable') (S0014).

F0093.statement: The /debug/search endpoint is exercised through create_app() with FastAPI TestClient, binding the debug API to the application's production app instance rather than a standalone server (S0014).

F0094.statement: The SciFact builder CLI implements 'download' and 'validate' subcommands; download calls download_archive then convert_archive into the output directory, prints corpus/query/judgment counts and dataset_hash, and writes manifest.json recording the archive's SHA-256 under source.archive_sha256 (S0015).

F0095.statement: scifact.download_archive and convert_archive both verify the archive against SCIFACT_ARCHIVE_SHA256, raising ValueError matching 'SHA-256 mismatch' on mismatch; download_archive leaves no scifact.partial file behind after a rejected download (S0015).

F0096.statement: scifact.convert_archive produces a deterministic normalized dataset (corpus ids like scifact-doc-10, queries like scifact-query-1, judgment relevance_grade 3) that load_dataset later validates, and includes a 'version=beir-2021-03-19-test-v1' marker in its summary (S0015).

F0097.statement: The SciFact subset builder `scifact.build_subset` is deterministic with respect to input order: it selects 30 queries by sorting on `sha256("scifact-subset-v1:{query.id}")`, so reversed corpus, query, and judgment inputs produce an identical dataset, as asserted by test_selection_ignores_input_order_and_retains_complete_judgments.

F0098.statement: build_subset preserves the complete set of judgments for the selected queries rather than sampling grades: the test asserts first.judgments equals all judgments whose query_id is among the selected 30 query ids.

F0099.statement: build_subset enforces size constraints: it rejects a source with fewer than 30 queries (ValueError 'at least 30') and rejects inputs requiring more than 500 required documents (ValueError 'more than 500').

F0100.statement: Subset output is a valid dataset that re-loads through `load_dataset`, yielding 500 corpus entries and 30 queries, and its manifest.source.license is propagated as 'CC BY-NC 2.0'.

F0101.statement: The scifact module exposes a CLI `main()` that parses a 'subset' subcommand with a `--source` option and writes to a module-level default `SUBSET_OUTPUT` path.

F0102.statement: A registered dataset name 'scifact-subset' is resolvable by the debug API: `selected_dataset("scifact-subset")` returns a corpus of 500 entries, coupling the scifact build output to DebugSearchRequest.dataset resolution.

F0103.statement: The evaluation corpus JSONL schema fixes a per-record identity contract of id + type ('document'|'chunk') + text, with optional document_id, title, and metadata; ids must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$ and no additional properties are allowed.

F0104.statement: The judgment JSONL schema requires query_id, target_type, target_id, and relevance_grade with grade constrained to the inclusive integer range 0..3, and forbids additional properties.

F0105.statement: The manifest schema pins schema_version to the constant 'evaluation-dataset-v1', purpose to 'evaluation', and requires source metadata that may include a 64-hex archive_sha256 and a license string.

F0106.statement: The manifest schema constrains `files` to exactly 3 entries whose path must be one of corpus.jsonl, queries.jsonl, or judgments.jsonl, each carrying a sha256 hash; this fixes the dataset's on-disk layout and integrity format.

F0107.statement: The query JSONL schema requires id and non-empty text, permitting optional category, expected_answer, key_facts (array of strings), and metadata_filters, so queries can carry filter and answer-grounding data alongside their text.

F0108.statement: Target identity in judgments and corpus/query records shares the same id pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$, so judgment target_id values are alignable with corpus id or chunk id values across schemas.

F0109.statement: build_subset depends on `load_dataset` for source reading and its output is expected to be re-loadable and schema-conformant, making the dataset loader the validation boundary for builder output.

F0110.statement: The corpus schema's `type` field distinguishes document-level and chunk-level records, and judgments likewise carry a target_type of document or chunk, indicating retrieval artifacts may be evaluated at either granularity.

F0111.statement: Tests for build_subset monkeypatch `scifact.load_dataset` and `scifact.SUBSET_OUTPUT`, indicating the builder depends on a module-attribute indirection for loading and for its default CLI output location.

F0112.statement: build_subset's selection algorithm and the debug API's dataset resolution are wired through distinct entry points (CLI and selected_dataset) that both terminate in load_dataset over the registered 'scifact-subset' dataset.
